title: Validate Brackets Outside Quotes
description:
Given a code snippet string `s` consisting of brackets `'('`, `')'`, `'['`, `']'`, `'{'`, `'}'`, double quotes `'"'`, backslashes `'\\'`, letters, digits, and spaces, determine whether `s` is structurally valid under string-literal rules:
- A double quote `'"'` outside a string literal opens a string literal, and the next unescaped `'"'` closes it.
- Inside a string literal, all bracket characters are ignored as plain text; a backslash `'\\'` escapes the immediately following character (so `'\\"'` does not close the string and `'\\\\'` is an escaped backslash).
- Outside string literals, all brackets `'()'`, `'[]'`, and `'{}'` must be properly matched and nested.

Return `true` if all string literals are closed and all outside brackets are validly balanced, otherwise `false`.
constraints: s contains only printable ASCII characters.
hints: Combine a boolean state (`inQuote`, `escaped`) with a standard bracket-matching stack.
While `inQuote` is true, consume escaped characters directly and only toggle `inQuote` on an unescaped '"'; at the end require both `not inQuote` and an empty bracket stack.

examples.explanation: The unmatched '(' and ']' sit inside the quoted literal and are ignored, while the outer '[' and ']' match.
Inside the string literal, '\"' is escaped so the string continues past ')', closes at the next '"', and the outer '(' matches ')'.
The string literal is never closed (the trailing '"' is escaped), so return false.
